summary: The standard clickable button control, with label, optional icon, and hover/pressed/focus states.
description: The Button control renders a styled, accessible button with a text `label` and optional icon. Its main product is the `onClick` signal; it also exposes its interaction state as boolean levels (`hoverState`, `pressedState`, `focusState`) for styling reactions, and an `enabled` input to disable it. Visual-state variants let hover/pressed/disabled styling be defined per state.
whenToUse: Any tap/click affordance with a caption. For a custom-drawn clickable area, a Group's `onClick` works; prefer the Button control when you want built-in states, label/icon layout and accessibility. The legacy `Button` type is superseded by this control.

ports.label: The button caption string.
ports.onClick: Signal; the click event — wire this to the action (Condition `eval`, Navigate `navigate`, Send Event `sendEvent`, …).
ports.enabled: Boolean level input; false renders the disabled state and suppresses `onClick`. The current value is also mirrored as an output of the same name.

runtimeBehavior: Declared-port-groups: icon ports appear when an icon source is chosen, and each visual state (hover, pressed, disabled, focused) contributes state-scoped styling ports. The catalog list is the superset; the editor shows the subset matching current parameters.
patterns: A boolean derived from form state → `enabled`: prevent invalid submits at the source.
antiPatterns: Simulating disabled state by hiding the button; drive `enabled` instead so layout and accessibility stay intact.
